physics_goals.quote: for CP violation discovery in the leptonic sector and, in particular, precision measurement of the CP violating phase δCP ... to the second oscillation maximum where, given the relatively high θ13 value, the CP violation signal is close to 3 times larger than at the first
physics_goals.value: Discover leptonic CP violation and make a precision measurement of the CP-violating phase δCP at the second oscillation maximum, using a long-baseline neutrino super beam made with the ESS linac

summary.plain: A proposed long-baseline experiment that would use the proton accelerator of the European Spallation Source in Sweden to make the most intense neutrino beam ever, aimed at a huge underground water detector in a mine 360 kilometres away, to look for differences between neutrinos and antineutrinos.
summary.technical: European Spallation Source neutrino Super Beam: upgrade of the 5 MW, 2 GeV ESS linac (doubled repetition rate, an accumulator ring compressing 2.86 ms pulses to 1.2 us, a target station), a 1 kt near detector on the ESS site 250 m from the target and a 540 kt water-Cherenkov far detector (two caverns, 1000 m deep in the Zinkgruvan mine, 360 km) aimed at the second oscillation maximum for leptonic CP-violation discovery. Conceptual design report 2022.
